records.summary: 429 Castro St is the historic Castro Theatre (City Landmark #100), currently operating as a movie theater with an accessory snack bar. The zoning district (NCD-CASTRO) treats a bar use on both the first and second stories as a conditional use, requiring Planning Commission authorization. The records show three prior applications at this address: two withdrawn telecommunications CUAs and one approved 2001 snack bar accessory use permit. The Castro Street corridor is exceptionally dense with bars and alcohol licenses—26 food/drink businesses and 19 active ABC on-sale licenses within 500 feet, flagging undue concentration risk.

Site is City Landmark #100 (Castro Theatre); alterations subject to Article 10 Certificate of Appropriateness
Live entertainment with amplified sound after midnight likely requires a Place of Entertainment permit from the Entertainment Commission
19 active ABC on-sale licenses within 500 ft; density proxy flags potential undue concentration under ABC's census tract analysis
Most recent use decision at this address (2001 snack bar) approved an accessory use to the movie theater, not a primary bar use
Two prior CUAs at this address were withdrawn (2001 telecom, 1999 telecom); no bar or entertainment CUA has been approved here
Within Central Neighborhoods Large Residence Special Use District; no specific bar restrictions but mixed residential context

comparables.why_comparable: Bar adding place of entertainment use in NCD-CASTRO, same zoning district, 186 m away on 18th Street corridor. Use decision (CUA) approved 2012. Nearly identical concept: entertainment accessory to alcohol service.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning Commission approved a place of entertainment as an accessory use to an established bar in NCD-CASTRO. This shows the Commission has accepted the bar-plus-entertainment pairing in this district when the bar use is already established or authorized. Filed March 2012, decided June 2012 (105 days).

comparables.why_comparable: Bar seeking extended hours at 465-469 Castro (57 m away), same NCD-CASTRO zoning, only denial found in the candidate set. Use decision (CUA) denied December 1994.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning Commission denied a CUA to extend operating hours for an existing bar on Castro Street itself. The only denial among the comparables signals that hour extensions—especially in a residential-adjacent NCD—face scrutiny. Filed September 1994, decided December 1994 (73 days to denial).

comparables.why_comparable: Modification of prior CUA for live entertainment in a restaurant and bar at 4109-4111 18th Street (156 m away), NCD-CASTRO. Use decision approved with midnight closing condition for live entertainment.
comparables.key_takeaway: Commission approved live entertainment until midnight in a full-service restaurant and bar, amending prior conditions. The midnight cap on entertainment hours was kept, showing the Commission limits late-night entertainment even when approving the use. Filed January 1998, decided April 1998 (77 days).

comparables.why_comparable: CUA for live entertainment at 4109-4111 18th Street (156 m away), NCD-CASTRO, approved 1996. Use decision shows entertainment approval on same block cluster as 2012.0205C.
comparables.key_takeaway: Commission approved live entertainment in the Castro NCD without extracted conditions in the record. The brief 66-day timeline (filed September 1996, decided December 1996) suggests a straightforward approval when the use fits the district character.

comparables.why_comparable: Bar expansion at 465-469 Castro (57 m away, same property that was later denied hour extension in 1994.517C), NCD-CASTRO. Use decision (CUA) approved July 1995.
comparables.key_takeaway: Commission approved expanding an existing bar and adding a bed-and-breakfast on the second floor at 465-469 Castro. This approval one year after the hour-extension denial at the same address shows the Commission will approve bar expansion but guards hours of operation. Filed April 1995, decided July 1995 (92 days).

comparables.why_comparable: Bar adding pool tables and live entertainment at 2367-2375 Market (97 m away), NCT-Upper Market zoning, approved 1992. Use decision shows entertainment added to existing bar in adjacent commercial district.
comparables.key_takeaway: Commission approved adding live entertainment and pool tables to an existing bar in the Upper Market NCD, 97 m from the Castro Theatre. The 259-day timeline (filed March 1992, decided November 1992) reflects older procedures, but the approval confirms entertainment-in-bars is authorized in nearby NCDs when conditioned. Adjacent district pattern.

comparables.why_comparable: Agency referral approving place of entertainment permit for an existing bar at 4067 18th Street (149 m), NCD-CASTRO, under Planning Code Section 715.48 which waives CUA when bar has been in regular entertainment operation. Approved 2011.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning approved a POE permit referral without requiring a new CUA under Section 715.48, which allows bars already operating entertainment to formalize it. This is an agency referral (one-day turnaround), not a use decision; it suggests a path for established venues but does not apply to a new bar use at 429 Castro.

comparables.why_comparable: Agency referral at 429 Castro Street (the subject property, 0 m), NCD-CASTRO, approved 2001. Snack bar approved as accessory use to the movie theater under Code Sections 715.46 and 790.64.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning approved a snack bar as an accessory use to the Castro Theatre movie theater in 2001. The approval was for a minor accessory concession stand, not a primary bar or entertainment use. This is the most recent Planning decision on record at 429 Castro and shows the building's use history as a theater with accessory food service only.

comparables.why_comparable: Bar expansion at 2342-2348 Market (183 m), NCT-Upper Market, approved 2008. CUA for expanding an existing bar with other entertainment into adjacent retail space.
comparables.key_takeaway: Commission approved expanding a bar with entertainment into adjacent space in the Upper Market corridor, 183 m from Castro Theatre. The 70-day timeline (filed April 2008, decided June 2008) and approval show bar expansions that add square footage are permitted when entertainment is already authorized and the expansion is infill. Adjacent district comparison.

comparables.why_comparable: Conversion of nonconforming bar to full-service restaurant at 465-469 Castro (57 m away), NCD-CASTRO. Use decision (CUA) approved April 1996, showing Commission supports food-service pairing with alcohol on Castro Street.
comparables.key_takeaway: Commission approved converting an existing nonconforming bar into a full-service restaurant at 465-469 Castro. The approval shows Planning favors alcohol uses paired with food service over standalone bars in NCD-CASTRO. Filed March 1996, decided April 1996 (50 days).

patterns.pattern: In NCD-CASTRO, Planning approved place of entertainment accessory to an established bar without extracted hour or operational conditions in the public record, but one nearby bar was denied a request to extend hours.

Live entertainment approvals in NCD-CASTRO commonly include closing-hour conditions; one restaurant-bar on 18th Street was limited to midnight for entertainment, signaling the Commission caps late-night hours even when approving the use.

Bars expanding into adjacent space or adding entertainment uses to existing bars have been approved by the Commission in NCD-CASTRO and NCT-Upper Market when the bar use is already authorized or nonconforming and the addition is accessory.

At 429 Castro itself, Planning has approved only an accessory snack bar to the movie theater (2001); no primary bar or entertainment CUA has been granted at this landmark address in the extracted record.
Two prior CUAs at 429 Castro (telecommunications installations, 1999 and 2001) were withdrawn before decision, showing a history of incomplete applications but no pattern of denials at the address.

Planning Code Section 715.48 allows existing bars in NCD-CASTRO that have operated entertainment regularly to receive a Place of Entertainment permit without a new CUA; this applied to one bar on 18th Street in 2011 but does not help a new bar application.

Conditional Use Authorization timelines for bar and entertainment uses in NCD-CASTRO ranged from 50 days (1996 bar-to-restaurant conversion) to 105 days (2012 place of entertainment accessory to bar) for approvals, and 73 days for the one denial (hour extension, 1994).

Existing bar expanding or adding entertainment within same footprint or into adjacent space

Application in NCD-CASTRO or NCT-Upper Market where conditional use has been granted to similar concepts

Concept characterized as intensifying use without clear establishment of the bar as existing/authorized before adding entertainment

risk.concept_summary: A bar with live entertainment and amplified sound, closing after midnight, occupying 24,138 square feet on the first and second stories of the Castro Theatre at 429 Castro Street in the Castro Street Neighborhood Commercial District.

overall.next_step: Request a zoning confirmation letter in writing from SF Planning stating whether the 24,138 square-foot size prohibits the bar use under Planning Code Section 715, or whether an exemption or variance path exists, before paying any application fees or signing a lease.

approvals.summary: Zoning does not permit the concept as described: the 4,000 square-foot size cap in NCD-CASTRO bars a 24,138 square-foot use, and intensifying the nonconforming nighttime entertainment on the second story is not permitted under Section 715.

findings.text: Planning Code Section 715 prohibits any retail or service use of 4,000 square feet or more in the Castro Street Neighborhood Commercial District, and this concept is 24,138 square feet.
A bar on the first story is a conditional use in NCD-CASTRO, and a bar on the second story is also a conditional use, both in force from March 7, 2022 under Ordinance 10-22.
Nighttime entertainment on the second story is not permitted in NCD-CASTRO under Section 715, in force since before January 1, 2022.

The space is described as continuing nighttime entertainment (the movie theatre remains alongside) and intensifying it by adding bar use. A nonconforming use in a Neighborhood Commercial district may not be significantly altered, enlarged or intensified without Conditional Use authorization under Section 186.1.

Section 715 records an exemption not evaluated by the rules: nonprofit, neighborhood-serving child care, schools, religious institutions, social services, community facilities or residential care may exceed 4,000 square feet by Conditional Use authorization. A bar does not fall under this exemption.

An earlier Conditional Use decision is on file at 429 Castro Street (1999.562C, approved March 23, 2000, for telecommunications equipment on the roof). The description does not say whether the proposal changes conditions of that approval.

approvals.summary: The description does not specify whether beer and wine or full liquor will be served, or whether a license will be new or transferred, so the rules cannot determine which ABC license type and process apply.

findings.text: The concept serves alcohol but does not state the type (beer and wine versus full liquor) or how the license will be obtained (new application versus transfer), so the ABC license requirements are not established.

Nineteen active ABC on-sale licenses are within 500 feet of 429 Castro Street, including six Type 48 bar licenses, six Type 41 restaurant beer-and-wine licenses, two Type 47 full-bar restaurant licenses, and two Type 75 brewpub licenses.

The density proxy (19 on-sale licenses within 500 feet) flags potential undue concentration; ABC's formal test compares on-sale licenses in the census tract with county ratio and crime reporting district data not shown in these records.
ABC license application referral to the SF Police Department and SF Planning Department is a step inside the ABC license approval; it is not a separate approval.

approvals.summary: A Place of Entertainment permit is required for live entertainment with amplified sound closing after midnight, and the Entertainment Commission holds a public hearing on the application after Police, Planning, DBI, Public Health and Fire Department review.

findings.text: Live entertainment with amplified sound that continues until after midnight requires a Place of Entertainment permit under Police Code Section 1060. The Entertainment Commission conducts a public hearing.

The Entertainment Commission sends the POE application to the Police Department, Planning Department, Department of Building Inspection, Department of Public Health, and Fire Department for review; these are review steps inside the POE permit, not separate approvals.

Planning approved a place of entertainment as an accessory use to an established bar at 4141-4149 18th Street in NCD-CASTRO in June 2012, 186 meters from 429 Castro, showing the Commission has accepted bar-plus-entertainment when the bar is already authorized.

A restaurant-bar at 4109-4111 18th Street (156 m away, NCD-CASTRO) was granted a CUA modification in April 1998 limiting live entertainment hours to midnight, indicating the Commission caps late-night entertainment even when approving it.

approvals.summary: A health permit to operate is required for a bar serving beverages to the public and is issued after plan check and inspection without a discretionary hearing, but the permit application is sent to Planning for zoning review.

findings.text: A bar or any business serving food or drink needs a health permit to operate, issued after plan check and final inspection.

The Department of Public Health sends the permit-to-operate application for a bar or restaurant to the Planning Department for zoning review; this is a review step inside the health permit, not a separate approval.

approvals.summary: A building permit with change of use is required because the concept changes from nighttime entertainment (movie theatre) to bar and nighttime entertainment, and the permit must conform to Planning Code zoning before DBI will issue it.

findings.text: The Planning Code use is changing from nighttime entertainment to bar and nighttime entertainment, which the rules determine is a change of use.

The description does not state whether the space will hold fewer than 50 people, so the proposed Building Code occupancy group (A-2 for 50+ assembly, or B for under 50) is not established. The existing occupancy group is not in public records.
A building permit application is routed to the Planning Department for zoning review, and the permit must conform to zoning before DBI issues it.
Tenant improvements, including installing bar equipment and any changes to the interior layout, need a building permit.

Planning approved a snack bar as an accessory use to the movie theater at 429 Castro Street on August 16, 2001 (MB0100732, filed August 15, 2001), the most recent permit on file at this address. The approval was for a minor concession stand, not a primary bar or entertainment use.

could_not_establish.question: Whether the 4,000 square-foot size cap in Planning Code Section 715 is absolute for a bar use, or whether a variance, exemption or interpretation exists that would permit a 24,138 square-foot bar in NCD-CASTRO.
could_not_establish.ask: SF Planning Department zoning counter or a pre-application meeting with Planning staff; request a written determination.

could_not_establish.question: Whether the Castro Theatre's existing nonconforming nighttime entertainment use on the second story can legally be intensified by adding bar service, given that new nighttime entertainment on the second story is not permitted under Section 715.
could_not_establish.ask: SF Planning Department; request a written determination of whether Section 186.1 allows intensification of a use that is not permitted for new establishments on that floor.

could_not_establish.question: What alcohol will be served: beer and wine only (ABC Type 41 or 42), or full liquor (Type 47 or 48), and how the license will be obtained (new non-quota application, or transfer of an existing license).
could_not_establish.ask: The applicant must decide the alcohol program and engage an ABC license broker if purchasing a quota license (Type 47/48).

could_not_establish.question: Whether the concept will occupy fewer than 50 people or 50 or more, which determines the Building Code occupancy group (B versus A-2) and the need for a Fire Department place of assembly permit.
could_not_establish.ask: Occupant load calculation on stamped architectural plans, reviewed by DBI and SFFD.

could_not_establish.question: Whether the existing occupancy group of the Castro Theatre's interior spaces matches the proposed bar and entertainment use, and what Building Code upgrades (exits, accessibility, fire separation) are required.
could_not_establish.ask: DBI plan check and a site inspection by a licensed architect or contractor; the existing occupancy certificate is not in public records.

could_not_establish.question: Whether the conditions of the March 23, 2000 Conditional Use authorization for telecommunications equipment at 429 Castro Street (1999.562C) remain in effect and whether the bar proposal would trigger a modification under Planning Code Section 303(e).
could_not_establish.ask: SF Planning Department; request the decision document (Motion) for Case 1999.562C and confirm in writing whether the new use changes any condition.

could_not_establish.question: Whether ABC will determine the census tract to have undue concentration of on-sale licenses, requiring a Public Convenience or Necessity finding from the city before issuing the license.
could_not_establish.ask: California ABC district office; the formal undue-concentration determination is made after the ABC application is filed and posted.

could_not_establish.question: Whether the proposal will be characterized by the operator as primarily a bar with accessory entertainment, or primarily entertainment with accessory bar service, because Planning and the Entertainment Commission may apply different standards.
could_not_establish.ask: The applicant and the applicant's land-use consultant or attorney; the framing affects which approval is primary and which is accessory.

expected_conditions.condition: Hours of operation limited to 6 a.m. to 1 a.m. or midnight, consistent with neighborhood norms in NCD-CASTRO.
expected_conditions.basis: One bar CUA modification in NCD-CASTRO limited live entertainment to midnight (4109-4111 18th St, 1998.034C), and one request to extend bar hours beyond neighborhood norms was denied (465-469 Castro, 1994.517C). The Section 715 use table shows principally permitted hours 6 a.m. to 2 a.m. and conditional hours 2 a.m. to 6 a.m., but the Commission has imposed earlier cutoffs in practice.

expected_conditions.condition: Security plan and good-neighbor policy required, including posting of security staff during operating hours, monitoring of the sidewalk and entry, and a protocol for addressing noise complaints.
expected_conditions.basis: One entertainment CUA modification (4109-4111 18th St, 1998.034C) referenced conditions relating to posting of employees during operations and patrol of the area after closing, standard conditions for bars and entertainment venues in residential-adjacent NCDs.

expected_conditions.condition: Soundproofing and acoustic isolation to prevent noise transmission to adjacent residential uses, likely including an acoustic study and mitigation plan as a condition of the Place of Entertainment permit.
expected_conditions.basis: Entertainment venues in mixed residential-commercial districts routinely receive sound-attenuation conditions; the Castro Theatre is a landmark with residential neighbors, and amplified sound after midnight raises impact concerns the Entertainment Commission addresses through acoustic conditions.

expected_conditions.condition: Certificate of Appropriateness required for any exterior alterations to the Castro Theatre building (City Landmark No. 100), reviewed under Planning Code Article 10.
expected_conditions.basis: Two prior applications at 429 Castro (1999.562C and 2001.0803C) both required Certificates of Appropriateness because the building is City Landmark No. 100. Any new signage, awning, exterior lighting or facade work will need Article 10 review by the Historic Preservation Commission.

expected_conditions.condition: No expansion of the bar or entertainment use beyond the approved square footage and no change in hours or entertainment type without a modification of the Conditional Use authorization.
expected_conditions.basis: Continuation-of-use referrals for bars in NCD-CASTRO routinely state no expansion without conditional use authorization (e.g., MB0600360, MB0900062). The Commission protects against incremental intensification by locking approved parameters.

expected_conditions.condition: ABC license conditions limiting service of alcohol to patrons seated at tables or the bar, and compliance with Responsible Beverage Service training for all alcohol servers and managers.
expected_conditions.basis: California AB 1221 requires RBS certification for every alcohol server and manager within 60 days of hire. ABC commonly conditions Type 42 and Type 48 bar licenses to prohibit sale to intoxicated persons, require ID checks, and limit service to seated patrons in entertainment venues.

filing_playbook.action: Request a written zoning determination from SF Planning Department on whether a 24,138 square-foot bar use can be authorized in NCD-CASTRO under any variance, exemption or code interpretation.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit a request for a zoning determination or schedule a pre-application meeting with Planning staff. State that the concept is a bar with live entertainment occupying 24,138 square feet on the first and second stories at 429 Castro Street, and that Planning Code Section 715 appears to prohibit uses of 4,000 square feet or more. Ask in writing: (1) whether the 4,000 square-foot cap is absolute, (2) whether any exemption or variance path exists, and (3) whether intensifying the existing nonconforming nighttime entertainment use on the second story is permitted under Section 186.1 given that new nighttime entertainment on the second story is not permitted. Request a written response before filing any application or paying any fee.

filing_playbook.action: If Planning confirms in writing that a path exists, form the legal entity, obtain the EIN, and register the business with the City.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File LLC Articles of Organization with the California Secretary of State ($70) and obtain the federal Employer Identification Number online from the IRS (same day, free). Then register the business with the SF Office of the Treasurer & Tax Collector to obtain a Business Account Number, required for all other City permits. Also file a Fictitious Business Name statement with the SF County Clerk if the public-facing name differs from the legal entity name, and publish the statement in a court-approved newspaper once a week for four weeks. The BAN, entity documents and FBN statement are prerequisites for the CUA application, the ABC license, and the health and building permits.

filing_playbook.action: File the Conditional Use Authorization application with SF Planning for the bar use and intensification of nighttime entertainment, if Planning's written determination in Step 1 confirms a path exists.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the CUA application to SF Planning with the project description, site plans, a community outreach summary, and the BAN. Frame the concept as a bar with live entertainment accessory to the bar, closing by midnight or 1 a.m., consistent with the 2012 approval of a place of entertainment accessory to a bar at 4141-4149 18th Street. Emphasize that the Castro Theatre is a neighborhood landmark, that the concept preserves the building's entertainment character, and that operating hours will respect residential neighbors. Expect neighborhood notification under Section 311, a Planning Commission hearing, and a 30-day appeal period.

filing_playbook.action: Apply for the Place of Entertainment permit with the SF Entertainment Commission after or in parallel with the CUA filing, but do not schedule the Entertainment Commission hearing until the CUA is approved.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Email the Entertainment Commission Deputy Director to confirm zoning eligibility and obtain the application packet. Submit the POE application online with the BAN, a copy of the lease or title, floor plans showing the performance area, a security plan, and a community outreach summary. Post a yellow notice at the premises for 30 days and conduct neighbor outreach. The Commission will refer the application to Police, Planning, DBI, Public Health, and Fire for review. At the hearing, present an acoustic study showing sound levels will not exceed residential noise limits, commit to hiring security staff during hours, and offer to close entertainment by midnight.

filing_playbook.action: Decide the alcohol program (beer and wine or full liquor) and engage an ABC license broker if purchasing a Type 47 or 48 quota license, or apply for a non-quota Type 41 or 42 if serving beer and wine only.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: If the concept will serve beer and wine only, apply for ABC Type 41 or Type 42. If the concept will serve full liquor, purchase an existing Type 47 or Type 48 license on the open market through a broker; San Francisco licenses cost roughly $100,000 to $450,000. Before applying to ABC, obtain the California seller's permit from CDTFA. ABC will post a 30-day public notice at the premises. If the census tract shows undue concentration, the city or Planning must provide a Public Convenience or Necessity finding before ABC will issue; start the PCN request as soon as the ABC application is filed.

filing_playbook.action: Submit the building permit application to SF Department of Building Inspection with stamped architectural plans for tenant improvements and change of use, after the CUA is approved.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Hire a licensed architect to prepare a plan set showing the bar layout, plumbing for sinks and bar equipment, mechanical for HVAC, electrical for lighting and amplified sound systems, accessible restrooms, and exit paths. DBI will route the application to Planning for zoning sign-off; Planning will confirm the permit matches the CUA approval. If the space is for 50 or more people, obtain a Fire Department place of assembly permit showing occupancy load, exit signage, and any required hood suppression. Schedule DBI inspections for rough framing, plumbing, mechanical, electrical, and final, and coordinate the final DBI inspection with the final DPH inspection.

filing_playbook.action: Apply for the health permit to operate with SF Department of Public Health after the building permit is approved and construction is at least 80 percent complete.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the health permit application online with the BAN, Location ID, federal tax ID, and a menu or description of beverages to be served. DPH will route the application to Planning for zoning sign-off; Planning will confirm the use matches the CUA. Schedule a pre-opening inspection at 80 percent construction complete and a final inspection before opening. Have a certified food safety manager on staff and all food handlers with California Food Handler Cards before the final inspection. The permit to operate is issued after the final inspection passes.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain ASCAP and BMI public performance licenses for playing recorded music and hosting live performances, and ensure all alcohol servers complete RBS training before opening.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Apply online for ASCAP and BMI blanket licenses at least two weeks before opening; the licenses are effective immediately and are required by federal copyright law for any public performance of music. Register each alcohol server and manager on the ABC RBS Portal, complete an approved RBS course, and pass the exam; the certification is valid for three years and must be on file at the premises for ABC inspections. Obtain workers' compensation insurance before the first employee starts and register as an employer with CA EDD within 15 days of paying wages.

timeline_cost.notes: No timeline or cost range is given because zoning does not permit the concept as described at this address: Planning Code Section 715 prohibits uses of 4,000 square feet or more in NCD-CASTRO, and the concept is 24,138 square feet. In addition, nighttime entertainment on the second story is not permitted under Section 715, yet the concept proposes to intensify the existing nonconforming nighttime entertainment use across two floors. If Planning confirms in writing that a variance, code interpretation, or redesign to under 4,000 square feet on the first story only would allow the use, the timeline to approval would be approximately 210 to 600 days and the government cost approximately $7,000 to $38,000. These figures assume approvals are granted; they are not times or costs to a denial or withdrawal. The size prohibition must be resolved in writing with Planning before any application is filed or any fee is paid.
